title: Ukraine attacks Russia with hundreds of drones - one of Kyiv’s largest assaults of the conflict | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Russia says it shot down more than 800 Ukrainian drones overnight in what appears to be among Ukraine’s largest aerial attacks on Russia, with authorities reporting at least six people killed.

The two sides have escalated their air war on one another, with Ukraine  increasingly firing barrages of drones at targets deep inside Russia, including warehouses and industrial plants as well as refineries.

Russia’s state-run TASS News said it was the largest Ukrainian drone attack since the beginning of the year – with many of the drones targeting the Moscow area where many of Russia’s elite reside.

Air defense forces and electronic warfare units shot down and neutralized 187 drones over the Moscow region, according to its governor, Andrey Vorobiev.

Geolocated video showed a huge fire at a Wildberries warehouse in the Moscow region, the Russian equivalent of Amazon. Vorobiev said no one was injured.

Wildberries’ warehouses have been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian drones in recent months. Ukraine says it has struck seven out of Wildberries’ ten largest logistics centers. The warehouse struck on Sunday was 250,000 square meters, the Ukrainian military said.

Kyiv has claimed that Wildberries handles supplies for the Russian military, and has stepped up its targeting of other critical parts of the Russian economy.

The company recently announced that it would build new warehousing in neighboring Kazakhstan.

One person, an 83-year-old man, was killed by a drone attack elsewhere in Moscow region on Sunday, according to Vorobiev.

Drones were intercepted over 17 regions – mainly in southern and western Russia – according to the Russian Defense ministry.

Five people were killed in the Rostov region in southern Russia, according to the governor of that region.

A “defense-industrial complex enterprise that produces solid rocket propellant” for various Russian weapons was struck in the attack in Rostov, according to the Ukrainian military.

On Sunday, maritime risk management agency Marisks said a Greek oil tanker had been attacked while positioned at a buoy mooring near Russia’s port of Novorossiysk. The company said the vessel was hit twice and Ukraine was likely responsible. But the weapon used, extent of the damage, condition of the crew and status of the cargo remain unconfirmed.

Russia meanwhile continues to target the Ukrainian capital Kyiv with a mix of missiles and drones.

Six people were wounded by strikes early Sunday, according to Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky. A book market in Kyiv was among the sites hit.

Kremenchuk and Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine were also struck by ballistic missiles, Zelensky said. Two people were killed in Kryvyi Rih and another in Sumy in the north, Zelensky said.

Thirteen employees of a steel factory in Kryvyi Rih were injured and one person died, according to Arcelor Mittal, which operates the plant. Rescue and search operations are ongoing, it said.

Ukraine did not shoot down any of the ballistic missiles fired at it overnight, according to an Air Force statement, again highlighting its short supply of missiles interceptors.

Russia fired more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided aerial bombs and 62 missiles at Ukraine over the last week, according to Zelensky.

“European interceptors cannot simply be allowed to sit in storage. Lives need to be protected. Russia must be stopped,” he added.

Elsewhere, an unidentified drone was shot down Sunday in Romanian airspace, according to the Defense ministry in Bucharest. The drone was intercepted by a Spanish F-18 fighter jet pilot on a NATO air policing mission.

It was the fourth drone shot down this year over Romania, the defense ministry said.

The ministry said its radars detected the drone entering the country from neighboring Moldova. Fragments appeared to have fallen in an uninhabited area between two villages.

In July, Romanian F-16 fighter jet pilots shot down three Russian drones breaching national airspace for the first time after dozens of such incursions in the more than four years of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.
